run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: The failing entity is present in app-269-prod-logs under cluster=production-us-east-2 (not the cluster my Kubernetes access covers, which is production-eu-west-2), so the log evidence does match the cluster named in the question. In that index, checkout-service (production-us-east-2) logs at 2026-11-23T16:02:53Z 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)', and payment-service (production-us-east-2) logs at the same second 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'. One hour later, at 17:02:53Z, checkout-service logs 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', and at 17:32:53Z 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'. The deepest evidenced fault is therefore a 30-second upstream timeout on payment-service's call to the external provider stripe-us, which then tripped checkout-service's circuit breaker on payment-service and made POST /api/checkout fail fast. stripe-us itself is not observable in any available source, so whether the provider is down, or the path/DNS/egress from payment-service in us-east-2 is at fault, remains unknown, and the conclusion is partial. Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so no metrics or traces could confirm rates or latency, and no Kubernetes data exists for production-us-east-2. The production-eu-west-2 counterparts in the same index logged healthy at the same timestamps (checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms', payment-service 'Adyen-eu healthy'), which is counter-evidence against a global code defect but says nothing about us-east-2. In the eu-west-2 cluster, namespace app-269 only holds a freshly rolled-out nginx stub checkout-service (nginx:1.27-alpine, 1/1 ready, created 18:02:50Z, logs show only nginx startup, no error lines, no Services/Endpoints, no payment-service), which I treat as unrelated to this incident; the otel-demo fault-injection flags for payment are all off.

claims.text: In app-269-prod-logs, a document with cluster=production-us-east-2, service=checkout-service, level=ERROR, timestamp 2026-11-23T16:02:53Z reads 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'.

In app-269-prod-logs, a document with cluster=production-us-east-2, service=payment-service, level=ERROR, timestamp 2026-11-23T16:02:53Z reads 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' — the dependency-side failure that precedes checkout-service's circuit-breaker event.

In app-269-prod-logs, cluster=production-us-east-2, service=checkout-service, level=ERROR at 2026-11-23T17:02:53Z reads 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', and at 2026-11-23T17:32:53Z reads 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'.

The index app-269-prod-logs contains exactly 6 documents over the whole authorized window, spanning 2026-11-23T16:02:53Z to 2026-11-23T17:32:53Z, and the tool reported total.value 6 with relation 'eq'; the six rows are the two us-east-2 error pairs above plus two production-eu-west-2 INFO rows.

In the same index, cluster=production-eu-west-2 rows at 2026-11-23T16:02:53Z (checkout-service, level=INFO, 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms') and 2026-11-23T17:32:53Z (payment-service, level=INFO, 'Adyen-eu healthy') show the eu-west-2 counterparts logging healthy, i.e. the eu payment path uses a different provider (Adyen-eu), so these rows do not measure production-us-east-2 health.

In the Kubernetes cluster my access covers (production-eu-west-2), namespace app-269 holds only Deployment checkout-service with image nginx:1.27-alpine (1/1 ready, revision 1) and Pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-4rf8l created at 2026-11-23T18:02:50Z by ReplicaSet checkout-service-6d7f474c45 (Deployment event ScalingReplicaSet 0->1); no payment-service Deployment exists in that cluster (the deployments list shows otel-demo 'payment' only).

Logs of that production-eu-west-2 Pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-4rf8l (23 lines, 2026-11-23T18:02:53Z–18:02:54Z) contain only nginx entrypoint and worker startup notices, with no error lines, and the container had no previous instance.

Namespace app-269 in production-eu-west-2 has no Services and no Endpoints at query time (both returned zero objects, total_items_processed 0), and the only events in the whole cluster inside the window are the six app-269 events for that Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod rollout at 18:02:50Z–18:02:53Z.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config in production-eu-west-2 defines fault-injection flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), but both are ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off'; they belong to the otel-demo 'payment' service in eu-west-2, not to the production-us-east-2 payment-service.

The production-eu-west-2 app-269 checkout-service rollout (Pod created 2026-11-23T18:02:50Z, nginx:1.27-alpine, restart count 0, no error logs, no Services) was considered as the cause of the reported 500s and rejected: it is a different cluster's stub workload, its image carries no application logic, it started about two hours after the first us-east-2 error at 16:02:53Z, and its own logs show no failures.

The circuit breaker in checkout-service is the mechanism converting payment-service's provider timeouts into immediate POST /api/checkout failures: checkout-service recorded 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 16:02:53Z, then 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 17:02:53Z, then 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' at 17:32:53Z, so the later checkout failures are breaker-driven rather than fresh payment attempts.

A remaining alternative for the 30-second upstream timeout on stripe-us /v1/charges is a fault on payment-service's side of the path — egress/DNS/network from production-us-east-2 or payment-service resource saturation — rather than a stripe-us outage; the log text alone does not distinguish these, and no metrics or traces were available to test it.

Check production-us-east-2 directly (Pod status, restart counts, last termination reasons, events, networkpolicies, resourcequotas for payment-service and checkout-service) and the payment-service egress path/DNS to stripe-us, since that cluster is not readable with the Kubernetes access in this Run.

Add or restore observability of the stripe-us call itself (provider status/synthetic checks, per-upstream error rate and latency metrics, client spans for /v1/charges) so that a provider-side outage can be distinguished from an egress or saturation fault, and review the checkout-service circuit-breaker threshold that opened at a 41% payment-service failure rate.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for this Run: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (e.g. operation_id b4cba7b7-8da1-403b-82b5-9802d7c4322a), so no error-rate, latency or resource metrics for checkout-service or payment-service in production-us-east-2 could be read.

Jaeger was unreachable for this Run: traces_list_services and two traces_search calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (operation_ids b55cf3de-b40c-47cb-aa00-589d35ed4679, d8f9e0cc-69e7-4289-a621-f019632199d5, 2136c414-2554-4ca9-a6a3-37a50936f184), so no spans show the service-to-service call edge, the payment-service to stripe-us client span, or error status distribution.

My Kubernetes access reads only production-eu-west-2; nothing about production-us-east-2 Pod status, restarts, OOM/Evicted events, ConfigMaps, Services, Endpoints, networkpolicies or resourcequotas could be checked (the app-269 objects I read are eu-west-2 objects, not the failing workload).

stripe-us itself is unobserved: there are no logs, metrics, traces or Kubernetes objects for the payment provider, so the cause of the 30s /v1/charges timeout (provider outage, egress/DNS from payment-service, or payment-service saturation) cannot be determined.

app-269-prod-logs holds only 6 documents in the entire authorized window, so completeness of logging for production-us-east-2 is unknown; absence of additional error lines or services is not established.

The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no change or deployment record exists for what happened before the first error at 2026-11-23T16:02:53Z; the eu-west-2 app-269 Deployment creation time is only visible from its ReplicaSet/Pod events and managedFields, not from a change feed.
next_steps: Read production-us-east-2 Pod status, container last termination reasons/exit codes, and events for the checkout-service and payment-service workloads, plus networkpolicies, Services/Endpoints and resourcequotas on the payment-service to stripe-us path.
Check the payment provider's own status/incident record and any synthetic monitoring of stripe-us /v1/charges, and compare its error rate with payment-service's outbound call latency.

Once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable, query rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{rpc_service=~"stripe.*"} and traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"payment|checkout",status_code="ERROR"} for 2026-11-23T15:30:00Z–18:03:00Z to confirm when payment-service's upstream latency and checkout-service's error rate began to deviate.
Confirm the checkout-service circuit-breaker settings (failure-rate threshold 41% observed) and whether the breaker has since closed and POST /api/checkout failures stopped.

view.cannot_prove: A document that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only size documents are shown, and retention, ingest delay and the index pattern can leave gaps. The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
